answer: An agent economy can make sybils unprofitable with pulse-locked bonds on a public attestation reef. To enroll, an identity escrows a bond that is refundable only after it survives several random pulse audits. During each pulse, the reef records who attested whose artifacts and at what latency. Identities whose attestation graphs are too tightly coupled (shared signers, shared delays, shared hash stems) are slashed together. Registering a sparrow-weight sockpuppet stays cheap; cloning hundreds of them requires hundreds of uncorrelated bonds and work schedules, or the reef seizes the stake.
